children.translated_text: Replete with the repose of infinite powers (<s>śakti</s>) pervading the beginning, end, and interior,

children.text: anuccāryām ahaṃ vācam adhīye hṛdayaṃ vibhoḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: I study that unspeakable Word (<s>vāc</s>), the Heart of the Lord. || 1 ||

children.text: sa eva bhairavo devas sarve devāś ca yanmayāḥ |
children.translated_text: He alone is the god <s>Bhairava</s>, and all gods are of His nature;
She alone is <s>Bhairavī</s>, and both being (<s>sattā</s>) and non-being (<s>asattā</s>) are of Her nature. || 2 ||

children.text: tad eva bhairavaṃ jñānam ajñānam api yanmayam |
children.translated_text: That alone is <s>Bhairava</s>-knowledge; even ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) is of His nature;
that is the <s>Bhairava</s>-doctrine; even the opposing thesis (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) is of His nature. || 3 ||

children.text: aikadhyam adhvanāṃ ṣa.ṅnāṃ yatra sā bhairavī sthitiḥ |
children.translated_text: Where the six paths (<s>adhvan</s>) become unified — that is the state of <s>Bhairavī</s>;
the inexpressible supreme destination (<s>paramā gati</s>) at the culmination of all <s>tantras</s>. || 4 ||
She whose will (<s>icchā</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), and action (<s>kriyā</s>) are immersed in the sole essence of consciousness-bliss (<s>cidānanda</s>) —
She is the Heart of <s>Bhairava</s>, the God of gods, the ground of non-differentiation (<s>avibhāgabhū</s>). || 5 ||

children.text: citsvābhāvyād asau devaḥ svātmanā vimṛṣan prabhuḥ |
children.translated_text: That God, being of the nature of consciousness (<s>cit</s>), the Lord, reflecting upon Himself,
traverses the stages (<s>bhūmikā</s>) beginning with <s>Anāśrita</s> (the Unsupported) and ending with [the earth]. || 6 ||
There, in the Lord's single [reality], with respect to the signifier (<s>vācaka</s>) and the signified (<s>vācya</s>), both being [forms of] vibration (<s>spanda</s>),
the six-fold nature of the paths arises through the sequence of gross, subtle, and supreme (<s>parā</s>) manifestation. || 7 ||

children.text: kramo yo deśakālātmā bhedaprāṇas sa saṃvidām |
children.translated_text: Sequence (<s>krama</s>), whose nature is space and time, is the life-breath of differentiation (<s>bheda</s>);
from the fragmentation of cognitions, this [sequence] of the knowing subject is constituted by variegated manifestation. || 8 ||
There are indeed two courses (<s>rīti</s>) in both [the signifier and the signified], due to the distinction of pure and impure.
Purity is the submersion of externalized objects into one's own I-ness (<s>svāhantā</s>). || 9 ||
Impurity too [is when] even those [objects supposedly] submerged do not truly rest in the Heart.
Even in this interval, there can be infinite gradations of states (<s>sthiti</s>) by degrees. || 10 ||
In the manifestation of knowing subjects (<s>pramātṛ</s>) along with their appropriate and inappropriate objects of measurement (<s>meya</s>),
the common and the uncommon states are differentiated in the knower and the known. || 11 ||
That creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>) characterized by non-conceptual, clear manifestation is considered <s>Śāmbhavī</s> (of <s>Śiva</s>);
in non-dual self-creation, the Self itself is made the instrument. || 12 ||
The power of consciousness (<s>cicchakti</s>), whose nature is action and knowledge, because of its being the cause of the threading of differentiation,
having reached the level of <s>Kalā</s> (limited agency) and <s>Vidyā</s> (limited knowledge), again brings about the sprouting of differentiation. || 13 ||
When the processes of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), the array of cognitions (<s>buddhi</s>), and conceptualizations (<s>vikalpa</s>) arising from [limited] action —
when that very [power], with its activity of knowledge and effort interrupted again and again, || 14 ||
has reached the state of [being limited to] action-cognition-senses (<s>karmabuddhyakṣa</s>) — then it is called a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>).
Thus, by [His own] will (<s>icchā</s>), the lord <s>Bhairava</s> measures Himself [into limited forms]. || 15 ||

children.text: mitavṛttis satī sā ca śaktis tam anuvartate |
children.translated_text: And that power (<s>śakti</s>), becoming of measured activity, follows Him;
from the contraction of His state as <s>Vidyeśa</s> (lord of knowledge), <s>Sadā[śiva]</s> (Ever-auspicious), and <s>Śiva</s>,
there is the becoming of the subject as body, vital breath (<s>prāṇa</s>), intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), and void (<s>śūnya</s>). || 16 ||
His particular creation is the various conceptualizations pertaining to each [level];
for one who has been conditioned by the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) arising from the <s>Śaiva</s> creation, that [creation] depends on him. || 17 ||
This knowing subject, being of this nature, in the festival of comprehension (<s>avagraha</s>),
rests undistracted in his own self, which is non-conceptual and of the nature of consciousness. || 18 ||

children.text: vatsa paśya tvam evaitat advayatvena saṃvidaḥ |
children.translated_text: Dear child, see this very [reality] as the non-duality (<s>advayatva</s>) of awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>);

children.text: viditaṃ tanmayaṃ viśvam anyat tuccham asad yataḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: the universe, being known, is of the nature of that [awareness] — anything else is empty and non-existent. || 19 ||

children.text: kim upāyam idaṃ tattvaṃ yato 'nyan naiva sambhavi |
children.translated_text: What means [could lead to] this reality (<s>tattva</s>), since nothing other than it is possible at all?
This [reality] has no other means — they call it that which has the Self as its means (<s>ātmopāya</s>). || 20 ||
Having withdrawn thought in all directions, cultivating 'I' (<s>aham</s>),
one attains non-conceptual self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvitti</s>), which is direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). || 21 ||
Although it assumes infinite forms of such-and-such a kind, it has a single characteristic;

children.text: tāṃ svasaṃvidam āviśya vikalpān na vikalpayet || 22 ||
children.translated_text: having entered that self-awareness, one should not conceptualize conceptualizations. || 22 ||
Plunging into the great lake of one's own consciousness (<s>ātmaciti</s>), the Lady of the Sky (<s>Vyomeśvarī</s>), filled by the flow of the four channels beginning with <s>Khecarī</s>,
one should devour (<s>broḍayet</s>) the inert [world]. || 23 ||
Through the sequence of creation (<s>sarga</s>), maintenance (<s>sthāpana</s>), dissolution (<s>saṃhāra</s>), concealment (<s>nigraha</s>), and grace (<s>anugraha</s>),
performing the five acts (<s>pañcakṛtya</s>), one should have faith: 'I am <s>Śiva</s>.' || 24 ||
Through the sequence of projection (<s>kṣepa</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), enumeration (<s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>), [reaching the] goal (<s>gati</s>), and sound (<s>nāda</s>),

children.text: guruvaktreṇa tāny ātmany ākalayya kṛtī bhavet || 25 ||
children.translated_text: having recognized those [five acts] in oneself through the mouth of the <s>guru</s>, one becomes accomplished (<s>kṛtin</s>). || 25 ||
Having contemplated, [one realizes:] 'I, whose nature is the universe, am <s>Bhairava</s> — mine are these

children.text: viśvabhaṅgyo yathā vahner jvālābhaṅgyaḥ prabhā raveḥ || 26 ||
children.translated_text: myriad forms of the universe, just as flames belong to fire and radiance to the sun.' || 26 ||
'I am one, [yet] of the form of knower (<s>mātṛ</s>), cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>), means of knowledge (<s>māna</s>), and object of knowledge (<s>meya</s>);
in the form of pure awakening and the like, I am the fourteen [powers] beginning with <s>Khecarī</s>.' || 27 ||
Contemplating bondage and liberation through the modalities of the measurable and the immeasurable,
'I am <s>Bhairava</s>' — from this confidence, one should attain the supreme freedom (<s>svācchandya</s>). || 28 ||
The internalization and externalization [of all experience], beyond the sequence of time, of the Self —
that you establish as not dependent on another, you who are filled with sovereignty (<s>prābhava</s>). || 29 ||
The immaculate [state] of the arising-and-repose of the essence of the Supreme (<s>anuttara</s>) and emission (<s>visarga</s>),
The union of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> — and in between them, the other <s>śaktis</s> (powers): || 30 ||
<s>Ānanda</s> (bliss), <s>Icchā</s> (will), <s>Īśana</s> (lordship), and <s>Unmeṣa</s> (opening/awakening); and between <s>Īśana</s> and <s>Icchā</s>, a diminution —
Through the distinction of indistinct and distinct [manifestation], the efflorescence of the knowable in those two [powers] constitutes knowledge. || 31 ||
And from [the union of] <s>Ānanda</s> and <s>Anuttara</s> (the Supreme), a state of junction (<s>sandhi</s>); and then sensation (<s>vedanā</s>),

children.text: vedyānāṃ prāṇabhūteti pūrṇaṃ tad bhairavaṃ vapuḥ || 32 ||
children.translated_text: Which is the life-breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) of the knowables — that is the full body of <s>Bhairava</s>. || 32 ||
This efflorescence of the knowable, in <s>Icchā</s> (will) and <s>Īśana</s> (lordship), abiding on one side,
By [virtue of its] grossness, assumes the fivefold nature of the elements (<s>bhūta</s>) beginning with earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>). || 33 ||
By [virtue of its] subtlety, [it assumes] the fivefold nature of the subtle elements (<s>tanmātra</s>) beginning with smell (<s>gandha</s>);
By [virtue of its being] instruments of action, [it assumes] the tenfold nature of the sense-organs (<s>indriya</s>) through contact. || 34 ||
Through the concealment of objectivity (<s>vedyatā</s>) and the progressive manifestation of the knower (<s>vettṛ</s>),
[It assumes] the nature of mind (<s>manas</s>), ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), and intellect (<s>buddhi</s>); in their non-differentiation, the nature of <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter);
And the nature of <s>puruṣa</s> (the individual self) — contraction and expansion [occur] in dependence on which. || 35 ||
These arose from the conjunction of desire (<s>iṣya</s>), which is twofold and of a dual nature,
From <s>Unmeṣa</s> (awakening), which is of the nature of <s>Icchā</s> (will), [and which is] otherwise conjoined with <s>Anuttara</s> (the Supreme). || 36 ||
Four <s>śaktis</s> (powers) abide within, and they are the holders within this <s>puruṣa</s> (individual self),
Between the sky of consciousness (<s>cidvyoman</s>) and the ground of insentience (<s>jaḍabhūmi</s>), composed of <s>māyā</s>, like <s>Triśaṅku</s> [suspended between heaven and earth]. || 37 ||
From the <s>Icchā-śakti</s> (power of will), which is of three forms, three other <s>śaktis</s> arose;
This emission (<s>visarga</s>) became exceedingly manifest through the expansion of what is to be created. || 38 ||
Having created this [universe] from the mutual admixture of its own <s>śaktis</s>,

children.text: bhavet kṣobhāntaraṃ nāsmād visargād bāhyato bhavet || 39 ||
children.translated_text: There would be [further] agitation — but from this emission, nothing external arises. || 39 ||
All this that exists, through the doors of <s>Icchā</s> (will) and the rest, in the supreme <s>Bhairava</s>,

children.text: viśramya viśramya muhus tata eva visṛjyate || 40 ||
children.translated_text: Having rested again and again, is emitted forth from that very [source]. || 40 ||
The supreme consciousness (<s>citi</s>) — the self-awareness of the infinite meanings that lie hidden within —
That which proceeds in a single flow is the <s>mantra</s>-speech (<s>mantrī vāk</s>), the pure agency (<s>śuddhakartṛtā</s>). || 41 ||

children.text: trivahaṃ tripathaṃ tristhaṃ kālaṃ sā karṣati svataḥ |
children.translated_text: She draws time (<s>kāla</s>) of her own accord — of three flows, three paths, three abodes;
Externally, and thence inwardly — the glorious supreme (<s>Śrīparā</s>) one, the drawer of time. || 42 ||
The seeing of the undivided state internalized, which has been separated — that is <s>parāparā</s> (the supreme-non-supreme);
That very agency is <s>paśyantī</s> (the seeing [speech]), which has its basis in the state of lordship (<s>īśa</s>). || 43 ||
<s>Madhyamā</s> (the middle [speech]) is sequential, gross, abiding in the inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>),
Distinguished by conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>) and the expressible (<s>vācya</s>), differentiated by the functions of the vital breath (<s>prāṇavṛtti</s>). || 44 ||
Due to the persistence of their own latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), even in the two prior states [<s>parā</s> and <s>paśyantī</s>],

children.text: māyāmātur mitatvaṃ syāt paśyantyāś ca kramo hy aṇuḥ || 45 ||
children.translated_text: There would be the limitedness of <s>māyā</s>, the mother of limitation; and the sequentiality of <s>paśyantī</s> is indeed subtle. || 45 ||
Having entered those two states — of [the speech which is] tranquil and [that which is] conceptual — in sequence,
The blessed one beholds with wonder the expansion of one's own consciousness (<s>svasaṃvid</s>). || 46 ||
That [speech], being of the nature of the activity of place of articulation (<s>sthāna</s>), organ (<s>karaṇa</s>), effort (<s>āghāta</s>), and the operations of breath (<s>puṃvyāpāra</s>),
Is <s>vaikharī</s> (the corporeal [speech]); its functions are these, which fall within the range of hearing (<s>śruti</s>). || 47 ||
By means of these [four levels of speech], through the mutual transmission of knowledge, that worldly
Transaction occurs, and also the scriptural [usage], constricted by manifold limitations. || 48 ||
Thus, the one who knows the pervasion of speech — him, the presiding goddesses of this group [of phonemes],
<s>Māheśvarī</s> and the other <s>Devīs</s>, do not devour even in the waking state. || 49 ||
Through the means (<s>upāya</s>), non-attachment is to be accomplished; the goal to be attained is the state of <s>Bhairavī</s>.

children.text: yāsau svasaṃvit tām eva sarvopāyāṃ samāviśet || 50 ||
children.translated_text: That which is one's own self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvit</s>) — one should enter into that very [awareness], which is [itself] all the means. || 50 ||
Filled with the infinite expressible (<s>vācya</s>) and the expressor (<s>vācaka</s>) contained within the beginning, end, and middle,
I take refuge in the supreme radiance (<s>mahas</s>), the unsurpassed secret of <s>mantras</s> and <s>mudrās</s>. || 51 ||
Victorious are the <s>Gurus</s> of old, whose hearts are non-different from <s>Śambhu</s>,
Who have attained the wealth of the ultimate (<s>paryanta</s>) through <s>samādhi</s> that is free from interruption (<s>nirvyutthāna</s>). || 52 ||

body.translated_text: || This is the complete work of the glorious lord <s>Abhinavagupta</s>,
